data.title: Robinhood Stock: Why Football Season Could Matter More Than Crypto
data.description:
Robinhood Markets (HOOD), the online brokerage, is getting more attention from investors as its prediction-market business grows and football season begins. The stock jumped 16.6% on Thursday to $124.72 after Wall Street analysts pointed to businesses that could make Robinhood less dependent on crypto trading. Prediction markets are especially important because Robinhood has already shown that customers are willing to trade event contracts in large numbers. The next major sports season could show whether this business can grow even further.

Catalysts that May Push the Stock Higher

Prediction markets are starting to become a meaningful source of revenue for Robinhood. In the second quarter, the company generated $156 million from event contracts, more than ten times the amount from a year earlier. That was higher than the $129 million Robinhood earned from equity transactions and the $100 million it generated from crypto transactions. Event-contract volume also reached 13.6 billion contracts during the quarter.

Football season could provide the next major test. Investment bank Piper Sandler (PIPR) raised its Robinhood price target to $145 from $135 this week because it expects NFL and college football to support another strong period for prediction-market activity. The firm believes that this business can stay active after the World Cup helped increase trading during the summer.

Promotion

Curious why XOVR invested in Kalshi? Explore the long-term strategy behind the investment.

Robinhood may also be able to keep more of the revenue from these trades over time. Its Rothera venture with Susquehanna International Group operates a regulated event-contract exchange and clearinghouse. That structure could reduce Robinhood's need to share revenue with an outside exchange, which would make each trade more valuable to the company.

Wall Street is also starting to see Robinhood as more than a trading app. Bank Morgan Stanley (MS) upgraded the stock to Overweight and raised its price target to $150 from $124. The firm believes that Robinhood can make more money from each customer through several different products instead of depending mostly on volatile retail trading activity. If prediction markets continue to support this thesis, then investors may become more comfortable valuing Robinhood as a diversified financial platform.

Risks to Watch Out For

However, Robinhood does come with risks, with the biggest one being regulation. For example, New Jersey has asked the U.S. Supreme Court to decide whether states should have the power to regulate sports-related prediction contracts. Although the case directly involves Kalshi, the final decision could also affect competing platforms such as Robinhood if states are given more authority over sports contracts.

Furthermore, the average HOOD price target of $127.43 per share implies that shares are trading near fair value. (See HOOD Stock Forecast).

data.title: IREN Stock Could Rally by Nearly 70% over the Coming Months — Here's Why
data.description:
Shares in Australian AI cloud firm IREN Limited (IREN) jumped by over 7% to $44.68 on Friday. This came as analysts reaffirmed their Buy rating on the stock and praised the company's AI cloud business. Analysts expect the segment to help boost IREN shares by 69.35% over the next 12 months. This is based on the average price target of $75.67.

On August 27, IREN released its fiscal Q4 2026 results. For the full year, the company reported AI cloud revenue of $128.8 million, up 687% from last year. During the quarter ended June 30, revenue from this segment also hit $70.5 million, up 110% year over year.

'AI Cloud Business Continues to Gain Momentum'

Interestingly, while AI cloud revenue grew rapidly, its overall revenue fell. Total revenue came in at $137.23 million, down by 27% from last year. In response, analysts maintained their Buy ratings, citing growth in IREN's AI cloud business.

Promotion

For instance, Citizens analyst Gregory Miller pointed out that the earnings show that IREN's "underlying AI cloud business continues to gain momentum." Miller maintained his price target of $80, implying about 79% upside.

Similarly, Bernstein analyst Gautam Chhugani, in his post-earnings note, argued that IREN has "aggressively executed across its cloud business." The analyst maintained his Buy rating on IREN shares and kept his price target at $100, implying about 124% upside.

Of note, IREN has already disclosed that it has secured about $2.8 billion in total contract value. The Sydney-based company has also sold out its capacity for calendar year 2026. The firm expects to reach more than $4 billion in annual recurring revenue by year-end.

Analysts Flag Other Growth Drivers

Beyond IREN's AI cloud business, analysts have also pointed to other factors driving their bullish projections. This includes IREN's strong pricing power.

For instance, H.C. Wainwright's Mike Colonnese reiterated his Buy call on IREN stock. Among other points, he noted that IREN is getting better prices for its GPU capacity.

Is IREN Stock a Good Buy?

On Wall Street, IREN's shares remain a Moderate Buy based on analysts' consensus rating. This breaks down into seven Buys, two Holds, and one Sell rating assigned over the past three months.

However, the average IREN price target of $75.67 implies about 69% upside (see IREN stock forecast here).

data.title: Astera Labs (ALAB) and Bloom Energy (BE) Soar as Investors Bet on S&P 500 Index (SPX) Inclusion
data.description:
Astera Labs (ALAB) and Bloom Energy (BE) rose about 11% and 7%, respectively, on Friday. The move comes as traders bet both companies could be added to the S&P 500 Index (SPX) later this month, according to a Barron's report. The index's quarterly rebalancing is set for September 21, with any changes expected to be announced after the close this Friday.

Investors see the clean energy hardware provider, Bloom Energy, as a prime candidate for the S&P 500 given its large market cap of over $63 billion and growing role in powering AI data centers.

At the same time, the high-beta AI connectivity provider, Astera Labs, has a market value of $47.6 billion. The stock is also jumping as traders believe that the AI buildout cycle is still strong, aided by its recent triple‑digit revenue growth and bullish analyst targets.

Promotion

Two ETFs for long or short leverage on BE

Companies often see a boost in their stock price when they join the S&P 500. This is because about 30% of the S&P 500 is held by index funds that must buy any new additions. Also, new inclusion signals strong market value and financial stability, boosting investor sentiment.

Which Other Stocks Can Be Added

Barron's noted that Cheniere Energy (LNG) and Everpure (P) are also potential stocks that can be added. Bloom and Cheniere both have market values well above the S&P 500's current minimum of $22.7 billion. Cheniere has been eligible for years and may finally get added, especially with energy stocks performing well in 2026.

Other possible candidates include Credo Technology (CRDO), Heico (HEI), Rocket (RKT), and Royalty Pharma (RPRX).

One company that will not be added is SpaceX (SPCX), as it must remain public for at least 12 months before S&P Dow Jones Indices considers it.

Who Might Be Removed

To make room for new members, the index typically drops companies with the lowest market values. Recent names near the bottom include:

  • Trade Desk (TTD)
  • Builders FirstSource (BLDR)
  • Norwegian Cruise Line (NCLH)
  • Molson Coors (TAP)
  • Mosaic (MOS)

data.title: Tyson Foods (TSN) Slips as Trump Targets Big Meat Processors With New Plan to Lower Beef Prices
data.description:
Shares of meat processing firm Tyson Foods (TSN) are down today after President Donald Trump said he is planning to sign a new executive order that's designed to lower beef prices. More specifically, he wants to give ranchers more ways to process and sell meat directly to consumers. The plan is to reduce farmers' reliance on the largest meat processors, such as Tyson, and increase access to smaller regional facilities. The move comes just days after Trump temporarily increased lower-tariff beef imports by up to 300,000 metric tons.

Trump said that ranchers should have more opportunities to sell their products without having to rely as heavily on the four largest beef processors. This shows how concentrated the industry has become. According to the White House, the four largest beef packers now account for about 85% of steer and heifer purchases, compared with 36% roughly four decades ago.

The order therefore directs the Agriculture Department to make it easier for smaller processors to gain federal approval. It also calls for more interstate sales of eligible meat and creates a new loan program to support small and regional processing facilities.

Those changes could give ranchers more options for where they process cattle and how they reach customers.

Trump Is Also Responding to Rancher Backlash

The new policy comes after another move to lower beef prices worried some U.S. ranchers. On August 26, Trump temporarily allowed 300,000 more metric tons of lean beef to enter the U.S. at lower tariff rates. The extra beef will be limited to 100,000 tons per month until November. The administration says the plan will increase the supply of ground beef and help lower prices. However, ranchers say cheaper imported beef could push down the prices they receive for their cattle.

In response, a separate order called for a review of beef labeling rules that show where the meat comes from. It also asks officials to reconsider protections for gray and Mexican wolves in areas where ranchers say wolves are harming their livestock.

data.title: Paramount Skydance (NASDAQ:PSKY) Stock Drops as Obscene Banner Declares Paramount's Relation to Trump
data.description:
We all knew that the merger between entertainment giant Paramount Skydance (PSKY) and Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) was starting to get downright acrimonious. For anyone who did not feel that way already, recent events drove that point home nicely as a plane towing an obscene banner behind it declared just how closely connected Paramount CEO David Ellison is to the Trump administration. Paramount investors found the whole thing distasteful, and sent Paramount shares down nearly 1.5% in the closing minutes of Friday's trading. Paramount has seen a 26.4% loss in its share price over the past year.

The Discourse is Getting Spicy

The plane in question flew over an event that featured two separate rallies outside the Paramount studio headquarters. One rally was in support. The other rally, meanwhile, was not. And the plane was clearly on the non-supporting side, as the banner it towed declared an unsavory connection between CEO David Ellison and President Trump. The banner was seen by multiple Paramount employees and photographed by them as well. Reports from The Wrap declared that the employees were not pleased about the banner, believing that the lawsuit in question was "…about antitrust, not politics."

A Streaming Resurgence

Meanwhile, Paramount is having a field day on streaming, noted a report from Screen Rant, as it has a new streaming win on its hands with the return of Scary Movie. This is the reboot version of the original 2000 release, and it is delivering some impressive numbers. In just one day after adding it to the library, the new release is currently Number 3 on Paramount's lists.

data.title: Ford Stock (NYSE:F) Gains, Looks to Sell 100,000 Fathom Trucks in the First Year
data.description:
There is something to be said for the power of audacity, and legacy automaker Ford (F) is going all in. Ford recently offered up sales projections on the Fathom electric pickup, and it plans to sell 100,000 of these in the first year. Ford investors were impressed, if guarded, and gave Ford shares a modest boost in Friday afternoon's trading. Ford has also seen a 22.74% rally in its share price over the past year.

Great Expectations, Ford Edition

If Ford can actually achieve this number, Ford would be the first electric vehicle maker that is not Tesla (TSLA) to clear the six-figure sales mark in one year for a single model. While General Motors (GM) managed to sell around 170,000 electric vehicles last year, that was spread out over all of GM's electric inventory.

The Fathom is designed to bring in drivers who are still driving gas or hybrid models, and will include a large touch screen as well as the BlueCruise hands-free driver-assist system, complete with Apple (AAPL) Maps integration. The Fathom will be selling in a tough market, though, as electric vehicles in the United States are on the decline since the government incentives were lost.

Promotion

High conviction TSLA bears now have this Tradr ETF

…Please Don't Ask About Towing

One problem for the Fathom, however, may come from its towing rating. Rather, it may come from the fact that Ford has not yet published such a rating. This is going to prove a problem for Ford's projection that those who are still driving gas or hybrid vehicles will make a jump to a pure electric.

One of the key points in that projection is that the Fathom can do everything that those gas and hybrid vehicles can. If it cannot tow a trailer, or handle a similar load, then it is useless as a work truck in some scenarios. And that makes the ability to pivot to the Fathom that much less likely for those buyers, limiting the earlier projections accordingly.
